how_read: Read the actual official Open Source Terms (including Acceptable Use) and https://docs.npmjs.com/policies/crawlers/ through the web reader. No website crawling is used by the capability.
findings: Acceptable Use 9: 'You may replicate data from the Public Registry using the Public APIs per this Agreement.' Use section 2 permits non-CLI software through public APIs. Website automation is separately restricted.

Acceptable Use 17 prohibits unreasonable load; five million requests in a month is an example of unreasonable load, not a quota. The crawler policy's one request/second concerns experimental WEBSITE crawlers, not a registry API allowance. Stop on 403/429; no retries or bypass.

Package content remains under its author's licence, not a blanket npm resale licence. Return the licence, registry package URL and published author/maintainer names for attribution, never contact details; preserve README markings except explicit truncation. No security/audit data (Conditions 4), or unrelated personal-data collection (Acceptable Use 4). Attribution does not replace package-specific licence obligations.

how_read: Read pypi.org/policy/terms-of-use (superseded February 25, 2025), followed its current Terms of Service and Acceptable Use links, and read docs.pypi.org/api/json/ and docs.pypi.org/api/ on the actual official pages.
findings: Registry metadata and API use are permitted subject to API terms. User-Generated Content 4 grants the PSF rights to copy and redistribute content unmodified on PyPI, not downstream rights. README and description text remain under each package's own licence; attribution does not grant rights. This permitted record is conditional on those package licences, consistent with config/vendors.yaml (conditional). Return only published attribution names, never contact details.
API Terms: 'Abuse or excessively frequent requests' may result in suspension. No spam or sale of user personal information. Published authorship is used only for package attribution, never outreach.

API introduction says no current edge rate limiting for JSON APIs, but reserves blocking irresponsible consumers. Requests are CDN cached, with ETag support; repeated high-volume consumers should use conditional requests/cache, identify their user agent, and avoid thousands of requests in minutes. This executor makes at most two serial requests and stops on blocks. No numeric JSON API quota is promised.

JSON API documents project and release endpoints. Release-specific responses omit releases; obtain the project response for latest version/history. Project releases is deprecated and may disappear. Description is uploader-provided metadata, not independently checked documentation.

how_read: Fetched the official API terms, Article 7's linked content terms at /riyokiyaku/, and their incorporated Digital Agency Public Data License 1.0. Read the v4 specification revision 1.2, overview and April 2022 published samples. No authenticated request made.
findings: Article 7 incorporates https://www.houjin-bangou.nta.go.jp/riyokiyaku/, which adopts https://www.digital.go.jp/resources/open_data/public_data_license_v1.0. PDL1.0 section 1 permits redistribution: 「複製、公衆送信、翻訳・変形等の翻案等、自由に利用できます」 and 「商用利用も可能です。」. Preserve source attribution and identify processing by Strale; third-party rights and logos are excluded.

Article 6 verbatim: 「このサービスは、国税庁法人番号システムWeb-API 機能を利用して取得した情報をもとに作成しているが、サービスの内容は国税庁によって保証されたものではない」. The overview at https://www.houjin-bangou.nta.go.jp/webapi/ instead says 「このサービスは、国税庁法人番号システムのWeb-API機能を利用して取得した情報をもとに作成しているが、サービスの内容は国税庁によって保証されたものではない」. Response attribution emits the Article 6 text plus the content-licence source and Strale processing credit.

Article 8(3) permits restrictions on concentrated traffic; Article 9(1)(3) prohibits 「短時間における大量アクセスその他本機能の運用に支障を与えること」. No numeric requests-per-time quota is published in these terms. API overview limits number lookup to 10 numbers and differences to 50 days; overview specification splits responses above 2,000 records. This executor performs one request per lookup, never retries or bulk crawls; HTTP 403/429 stop. HTTP 404 means an invalid/unregistered app ID, not company-not-found. Article 9 prohibits disclosure/lending of the ID.

how_read: Official copyright notice fetched via web open, including General principles and Exceptions; candidate list checked on the EU enlargement page.
findings: Commission Decision 2011/833/EU authorises commercial reuse with source acknowledgement, subject to individual notices and these exceptions; this record covers only the restricted eurostat-data executor.

(a) Data identified as belonging to sources other than Eurostat and third-party copyrighted material are excluded: refuse non-Eurostat source declarations and unrecognised rights notices in returned JSON-stat source/extension/annotations. SOURCE_INSTITUTIONS and other explicit source anchors are checked; DISSEMINATION_SOURCE_DATASET annotations identify lineage, not ownership. Separately linked ESMS documents and catalogue notices are not inspected; missing declarations are reported as an output limitation. No third-party documents are returned.

(b) Data for countries outside EU/EFTA/official acceding and candidate countries are excluded. Round 5 uses EUROSTAT_ALLOWED_DATASETS: a curated Eurostat-sourced dataset list audited against live JSON-stat metadata on 2026-10-26 (recorded in __fixtures__/eurostat/dataset-audit-2026-10-26.json). The sole geographic dimension must be geo; partner/citizen/birth/residence/load/unload/origin/destination/control/counterpart/vessel-nationality tables are excluded. The audit conservatively rejects every non-geo/time code matching ISO alpha-2 or a country-prefix NUTS shape, including non-geographic collisions; this necessarily narrows coverage of requested families. There is no runtime country-content detection outside geo. Require geo and accept only exact EU/EFTA/official candidate countries, their NUTS regions (country prefix plus 1–3 letters/digits), and supported EU/EFTA/euro-area aggregates. Potential candidate Kosovo is excluded. Retain post-fetch geo dropping/counting and label-aware defence in depth only for geo. Omit excluded labels. Other datasets return dataset_not_supported with the supported list and instructions to request an addition through Strale support; additions require metadata and terms review. This implements the country restriction without trying to infer geographic meaning in arbitrary codelists.

(c) Liechtenstein and Switzerland declaring-country trade data from 1995 under HS, SITC, BEC, NSTR and national classifications are excluded. Austria declaring-country CN8 trade data are also excluded: the curated list excludes international trade; retain defence-in-depth refusal through the executor's dataset-prefix, title/theme/category and trade-lineage rules. Domestic retail trade, wholesale trade, distributive trade and trade sector phrases are exempt; international/foreign/extra-EU/intra-EU trade remains refused. A stk_flow dimension also triggers refusal (including nrg_stk_gas). Source-key rules inspect dataset metadata, not data.dimension ids/categories such as owner.

Logos and trademarks are excluded; the executor returns statistical codes, labels and observations only, with no logos or publications. Modifications must be declared with a non-responsibility disclaimer: every output includes the dataset DOI (10.2908/CODE), access date, acknowledges Eurostat and the Commission Decision and states Strale flattened the data and Eurostat is not responsible for the rendering.
decision_ref: DEC-20261023-A; orchestrator approval 2026-10-26 scoped to commercial-permitted Eurostat data

how_read: Rendered https://ares.gov.cz/stranky/open-data, /stranky/vyvojar-info and /stranky/podminky-provozu in a headless browser with an honest user agent (robots.txt disallows only /cms/, which was not fetched), and re-read the operating conditions on mf.gov.cz/cs/ministerstvo/informacni-systemy/ares. The two ARES pages are the ones the Ministry's reply links. The reply itself is the MF ČR reply of 2026-10-29 to petter@strale.io (Jan Sadlik, ICT, MF ČR), relayed from Petter's mailbox; it is not archived in the repository.
findings: MF ČR reply of 2026-10-29 to petter@strale.io, answering the 2026-10-26 request about per-call commercial reuse with attribution: information published through ARES may be reused under the ARES operating conditions and the Czech law on free access to information (open data). MF gives no individual legal assessment; the user is responsible for compliance.

Open-data page: MF publishes the company-register basics (name, dates of creation, dissolution and extinction, seat, IČO, purpose, statutory body members with addresses and dates, register designation) as open data under Government Regulation 425/2016 and Act 304/2013 § 7. It quotes Act 106/1999 § 3: open data are 'informace … jejichž způsob ani účel následného využití není omezen' (information whose manner and purpose of further use is not restricted).

Open-data page, conditions: 'data lze využívat v souladu s podmínkami provozu IS ARES' (data may be used in line with the ARES operating conditions); MF is not the data's author and is not liable for completeness, correctness or damage from further use; 'Ministerstvo financí nepovažuje za vhodné modifikovat data způsobem, který by zkresloval jejich význam, bez uvedení, že tomu tak bylo učiněno' (MF does not consider it appropriate to modify the data in a way that distorts its meaning without saying so).

Developer page and operating conditions: 'Služby může využívat každý, pokud bude respektovat podmínky provozu' (anyone may use the services if they respect the operating conditions). MF may restrict users who send more than 500 queries a minute, repeat identical or invalid queries, run many parallel automated queries, spread queries over many IP addresses to evade limits, or probe the database with random values. All ARES data is informative only and is not an official document ('nemají charakter úřední listiny').

No page states a required attribution wording. The mf.gov.cz page disclaims responsibility for other portals that show ARES data 's odkazem na zdroj údajů z ARES' (citing ARES as the source); Strale names ARES and MF ČR as the source on every response, says the data is informative only, and does not alter returned values. Not established: whether every field cz-company-data returns falls inside the published open-data list; the reply covers information published through ARES generally.

how_read: Written reply from support@serper.dev on 2026-10-27 19:40 CET to Petter's email of 2026-10-26 asking whether per-call resale is permitted; read from the inbox by the 2026-10-28 morning run (docs/company/OUTBOX.yaml serper-resale-terms). The published terms ("Updated on May 29, 2024", read 2026-10-26) are silent on resale.
findings: Serper, in writing: "Using Serper as an upstream source within a value-added commercial service is permitted under our standard terms. This includes returning processed results through your own per-call API."

Condition: reselling API access without added value is not permitted — every executor must return processed results in Strale's own schema, one search per request, never Serper's response passed through as-is.
No separate reseller or partner agreement; standard prepaid tiers apply.
The permission does not grant third-party rights; Serper points to Google's terms (the search-data case DEC-20261023-A already allows for in the vendor lane).

permission.condition: Value-added processed results in Strale's own schema, one search per request; never raw API access resold. No third-party (Google) rights are granted.
reopen_only_if: Serper revokes or narrows the permission in writing
Serper's published terms change to prohibit it
a third party (for example Google) makes a claim against Strale over this use

how_read: jina.ai was unreachable from the 2026-10-24 session. Read instead: the reader's open-source code (github.com/jina-ai/reader, src/api/crawler.ts, src/dto/crawler-options.ts) and search summaries of jina.ai pages.
findings: Jina's sales FAQ (per search summary) says hosted-API commercial use is covered by its service terms for signed-up, paying users; Strale called it keyless, on the anonymous tier, whose terms were never recorded.
The hosted reader retries a non-200 fetch through its own rotating proxy pool unless X-Proxy: none is sent, and does not report the target's status — DEC-20261023-A never lane item 2.
Removed from every fetch path on 2026-10-24 (PR #723); listed in PROHIBITED_UPSTREAM_HOSTS so it cannot return.
